data.title: Cyclone Akvan: Odisha evacuates over 300K people, 47 trains cancelled
data.description:
Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi conducted another comprehensive review of the preparedness and response measures for the impending Cyclone 'Akvan'.

​According to the official release, detailed discussions were held regarding cyclone readiness.

All necessary steps are being taken in close coordination among the state administration, district administrations, and concerned Central Government departments to achieve the 'Zero Casualty' target. Expressing strong confidence, the Chief Minister stated that with the blessings of Mahaprabhu Shri Jagannath, this goal will certainly be accomplished.

​Briefing the media following the review meeting, the Chief Minister informed that according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD), Cyclone 'Akvan' is likely to make landfall on Friday afternoon at Haripur, near Gopalpur.

 

​Extensive preparedness and mitigation measures have been undertaken across 20 districts of the state to tackle the situation.

​So far, more than 300,000 people have been evacuated to safe locations. Additionally, 4,170 pregnant women have been shifted to safe shelters, out of whom 1,317 women have given birth to newborn babies, the Chief Minister stated.

​While a total of 9,341 cyclone shelters have been kept ready across the state, 2,623 of them have already been made operational.

​For rapid field-level response, a total of 418 teams have been deployed. These include 60 ODRAF teams, 14 NDRF teams, 216 Fire Service teams, and 128 tree-cutting teams from the Odisha Forest Development Corporation (OFDC). Furthermore, an additional 28 Fire Service teams have been kept on standby.

​To ensure uninterrupted telecommunication during the cyclone, arrangements have been made for 17 satellite phones, Cells on Wheels (CoW), and telecom backup systems.

​Meanwhile, through ORSAC, a total of 941 landslide-prone villages have been identified across 6 districts- Ganjam, Gajapati, Rayagada, Kandhamal, Malkangiri, and Koraput. Arrangements have been put in place to evacuate residents from these villages to safer locations. Most of the people evacuated in Kandhamal and Gajapati districts belong to these landslide-prone areas.

​Responding to media queries regarding some fishermen from Andhra Pradesh stranded near the Odisha coast, the Chief Minister said that all arrangements have been made for their safety with the assistance of the Indian Coast Guard, and steps are underway to bring them safely to Ganjam district.

​During the review, the Chief Minister spoke over the phone with the Puri District Collector to inquire about the ground situation and preparedness, advising him to pay special attention to the safety of the Habishyalis (elderly women observing Kartika rituals).

​The Chief Minister also informed that 47 trains have been cancelled, and 28 trains have been rescheduled.

​Clarifying that the Coast Guard and the Rail Coordination Cell remain active for emergency rescue operations, the Chief Minister reiterated that all departments are on high alert and fully prepared, giving top priority to the safety of the people of the state.

​Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari was present during the review meeting. Chief Secretary Anu Garg, Additional Chief Secretary (Revenue Department) Arabinda Padhee, Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh Pravakar Patil, along with Principal Secretaries and Secretaries of various departments, were also in attendance.

data.title: Cyclone Akvan weakens, likely to cross Odisha coast near Gopalpur today
data.description:
The India Meteorological Department (IMD) on Friday said that Cyclone Akvan had weakened into a cyclonic storm over the westcentral Bay of Bengal and is likely to cross the North Andhra Pradesh-South Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur by forenoon, with maximum sustained wind speeds of 70-80 kmph, gusting to 90 kmph.

According to the IMD, the system moved north-northwestwards at a speed of 21 kmph during the past six hours and lay centred over the westcentral Bay of Bengal at 2:30 AM on Friday.

The cyclonic storm was located near latitude 17.7°N and longitude 84.9°E, about 110 km southeast of Kalingapatnam in Andhra Pradesh, 170 km east of Visakhapatnam, 170 km south of Gopalpur in Odisha, 250 km south-southwest of Puri and 370 km east-northeast of Narsapur in Andhra Pradesh.

 

The IMD said the system was likely to continue moving north-northwestwards before crossing the North Andhra Pradesh-South Odisha coasts close to Gopalpur by forenoon on Friday.

Latest satellite imagery indicated that land interaction had commenced as the sheared cloud mass associated with Cyclone Akvan entered the North Andhra Pradesh-South Odisha coastal region.

The weather system is under continuous surveillance by the Doppler Weather Radars at Visakhapatnam and Gopalpur.

Meanwhile, Odisha Chief Minister Mohan Charan Majhi spent more than two-and-a-half hours, from around 11 PM to 1:30 AM, at the Special Relief Commissioner's (SRC) office reviewing the evolving situation as the cyclone approached the coast.

During the review, the Chief Minister held direct consultations with officials and directed them to ensure that all necessary assistance reached residents while making every effort to achieve the zero-casualty target.

He returned to his residence at around 1:35 AM amid rainfall.

The pre-landfall impact of Cyclone Akvan began to be felt in Bhubaneswar around 1 AM, with heavy rainfall accompanied by gusty winds. With landfall expected around noon on Thursday, authorities said pre-storm conditions were already affecting the state capital.

Revenue and Disaster Management Minister Suresh Pujari, Chief Secretary Anu Garg, Additional Chief Secretary and Revenue Secretary Arabinda Padhee, Special Relief Commissioner Rajesh Prabhakar Patil, Fire Services Director General Sudhanshu Sarangi and several senior officials also held discussions with district administrations in cyclone-affected areas.

Most officials remained at their respective offices overnight to monitor the situation and evacuation efforts, including the shifting of residents from vulnerable areas to safer shelters.

data.title: AI sell-off hits Indian smallcaps; Sterlite, HFCL down up to 29% in a month
data.description:
The global sell-off in artificial intelligence (AI) stocks has also shifted focus to Indian companies linked to the AI ecosystem. According to an analysis by Business Standard, smallcap stocks linked to the US data-centre and AI investment boom have come under significant selling pressure over the past one month, moving in tandem with the Nasdaq Composite index, which has declined 7.5 per cent.
 
Analysts warn that the sharp rally in several such stocks may have left valuations stretched, making them vulnerable to corrections amid the global reassessment of AI-related investments.
 
The stocks under coverage that have delivered handsome returns over the past year have one thing in common -- exposure to the US data-centre boom. These include Sterlite Technologies (STL), HFCL, Aditya Infotech, Sansera Engineering, Acutaas Chemicals, Welspun Corp, Netweb Technologies and MTAR Technologies. 
 
Sterlite Tech, HFCL down up 29% in 1 month 
Exchange data, as of November 18, showed that Sterlite Technologies shares have declined 27 per cent in the past month, although its one year return stood at 481 per cent. Similarly, HFCL shares have fallen 29 per cent in a month but gained 159 per cent over a year.
 
Welspun Corp and MTAR Technologies shares declined 15 per cent and 17 per cent, respectively, over the past month. However, they gained 145 per cent and 130 per cent, respectively, over one year.
 
Netweb Technologies shares have slipped 11 per cent over the past month (up 29 per cent in 1 year). E2E Networks shares have declined 24 per cent in a month but remain up 96 per cent over the past year.
 
Why are AI stocks under pressure? Analysts said that as AI investments face growing scrutiny in the US, concerns over valuations, debt-funded capital expenditure and the sustainability of spending by large technology companies may spill over to Indian companies linked to the global AI and data-centre ecosystem.
 
However, there are few exceptions. Data showed that Aditya Infotech shares remained largely unchanged over the past month, while gaining 133 per cent over one year. Sansera Engineering shares rose 13 per cent in a month and 197 per cent over a year. Acutaas Chemicals gained 22.5 per cent over the past month and its one year return stood at 132 per cent. 
'Anti-AI trade' 
Apoorva Khandelwal, research associate at Anand Rathi Institutional Equities, said the correction in several stocks is largely a reflection of the emerging 'anti-AI trade', as investors become increasingly concerned about debt-funded AI capex, pressure on hyperscalers' free cash flows and rising financing costs. There are also concerns around tighter regulations, power availability and potential delays in data-centre projects in the US, which could slow the pace of AI infrastructure spending.
 
"Indian companies exposed to this theme, particularly in optical fibre and data centre infrastructure, are vulnerable as valuations have already factored in strong growth expectations," he said. Sterlite Tech, HFCL order books
 
The order books of some companies highlight their significant exposure to the AI and data-centre ecosystem. Sterlite Technologies' order book has expanded 4.6-fold since March to about ₹35,274 crore, supported by $1.2 billion (approximately ₹11,400 crore) in deals with hyperscalers, or large cloud and technology companies operating extensive data-centre networks.
 
According to HFCL's management, a large portion of its roughly ₹18,500 crore fibre and data-centre order book comes from hyperscalers. 
'Underlying opportunity intact' 
Despite the recent correction, Vinit Bolinjkar, head of research at Ventura, believes the underlying opportunity remains intact, and that investors should distinguish between companies with direct exposure to AI infrastructure spending and those benefiting indirectly from the broader data-centre investment cycle.
 
He said that Netweb trades at approx 60-65 times trailing earnings, E2E Networks at around 90 times and Black Box at approximately 65 times. "Such multiples leave limited room for execution delays, margin pressure or earnings disappointments," he said.

data.title: IndiGo expands Southeast Asia flights from Delhi ahead of year-end holidays
data.description:
IndiGo, one of India's biggest airlines and one of the fastest-growing carriers in the world, has announced expansion of its Southeast Asia connectivity from Delhi, ahead of the year-end holidays.

According to the official release, IndiGo will launch daily, non-stop flights between Delhi and Kuala Lumpur, Malaysia, from December 20, additional daily frequency between Delhi and Singapore, from December 20, increasing services to 14 departures weekly and an additional 5x weekly frequency between Delhi and Bangkok, from December 28, increasing services to 19 departures weekly IndiGo currently operates direct flights to Kuala Lumpur from Bengaluru and Chennai.

With over 50 weekly flights connecting Delhi to Thailand, Singapore, Vietnam and Indonesia, the airline has steadily expanded its Southeast Asia footprint from the capital. The addition of Kuala Lumpur to Delhi's network, along with increased frequencies to Singapore and Bangkok, further reinforces Delhi's position as a key international hub while deepening connectivity between India and Southeast Asia's leading travel, business and trade markets.

 

Customers can plan and book their travel through IndiGo's official website www.goIndiGo.in, mobile app, or authorised travel partners. They can also pre-book their meals and beverages, including alcoholic beverages.

Additionally, they can personalise their travel experiences by opting for offerings that suit their respective preferences, including UpFront and Flexi, which give the best value, comfortable seats, complimentary snacks, and hassle-free adjustment to itineraries. IndiGoStretch, the airline's business cabin, is available on flights from Delhi to Singapore and Bangkok.

IndiGo is India's preferred and among the fastest-growing carriers in the world. IndiGo has a simple philosophy: offer fares that are affordable, flights that are on time, and provide a courteous and hassle-free travel experience across its unparalleled network.

With its fleet of 430+ aircraft, the airline operates nearly 2200 daily flights, connecting 95+ domestic and 40+ international destinations, and welcomed more than 123 million customers in FY26.

IndiGo was recognised as the 'Best Low-Cost Airline in India & South Asia' at the 2026 Skytrax World Airline Awards, while also earning accolades for 'Best Cabin Crew in India & South Asia' and being named the 'Cleanest Airline in India & South Asia'. IndiGo was also named the sixth Most Punctual Airline in Asia-Pacific in 2025 by the global aviation analytics firm, Cirium.

data.title: Base, precious metals meltdown; dollar dominance holds key: Julius Baer
data.description:
Disclaimer: This article is written by Carsten Menke, Head of Next Generation Research, Julius Baer. Views expressed are his own. Readers' discretion is advised. Flows are dominating fundamentals in the industrial and precious metal markets, putting broad-based pressure on prices since the start of the week. Speculative traders and trend followers in the futures markets appear to be parting with their positions as they fear further interest rate increases by the US Federal Reserve and an even stronger US dollar.
 
Since we expect inflationary pressure in the US to soften, the US dollar should weaken, and investors should return to the metal markets. We stick to our established views for now. Buying opportunities could open up for silver and copper should prices fall further.
 
 
There has been broad-based pressure in the metal markets during the past few days. Gold and silver are down around 3 per cent and 7 per cent since the start of the week, while aluminium and copper have lost about the same. Since these metals belong to very different corners of the commodity universe, the moves seem much more driven by flows than fundamentals. 
  
Our view on US monetary policy remains unchanged: Inflationary pressure in the US should soften on the back of easing energy prices, allowing the Federal Reserve to be less aggressive than currently expected.
 
Looking ahead to 2027, a shift in expectations towards fewer or no interest rate hikes should weigh on the US dollar while luring investors back into the metal markets. As a result, gold and silver prices should start to recover.
 
For now, we remain Constructive on gold and Neutral on silver. A buying opportunity might be opening up for silver should prices fall towards or below USD 45 per ounce and the gold/silver ratio at the same time rise towards or above 85.
 
Since copper is much less of a monetary metal than gold and silver, its price performance does not depend that strongly on the outlook for US monetary policy. 
 
Our long-term view on copper is unchanged. We still see the market at risk of slipping into a structural deficit. While initially based on insufficient supplies, our conviction in long-term demand growth has increased. Copper is an electrification enabler, with demand increasingly being driven by technologies such as electric vehicles, clean energy, and related on-grid battery storage systems.
 
Artificial intelligence is adding to this trend, but it is not driving it. We stay Neutral for now, waiting for prices to find a bottom. Prices trading below USD 13,000 per tonne could be considered an attractive longer-term entry point. Selling by investors remains the biggest short-term risk for all of the metals, again stressing the dominance of flows over fundamentals at the moment.

data.title: Trump's cyber chief Sean Cairncross to step down amid repeated tech outages
data.description:
In what is being described as a direct fallout of the consistent outages plaguing tech services in the US, President Donald Trump's National Cyber Director Sean Cairncross is stepping down from his post, Fox News has confirmed.

His departure comes following disruptions involving Microsoft Outlook, United Airlines, major banks and the NSA, along with a nationwide FAA ground stop. Fox News cited an official who said that Cairncross does not want to serve another two years in the role, though his departure date remains unclear.

Caincross' reported exit came despite Trump urging Americans not to panic or stockpile emergency supplies following a string of high-profile technology and banking disruptions across the United States, insisting the incidents are isolated technical glitches rather than a coordinated cyberattack.

 

Speaking in an interview with Fox News ahead of the APEC Summit, Trump was asked about growing public anxiety, including reports of people stockpiling food and water, prompted by the recent outages and his earlier declaration of a national emergency over the US power grid.

The president brushed off the concerns, characterising the disruptions at major institutions like JPMorgan Chase as routine, unrelated occurrences amplified by media coverage.

"Tell them to relax. Everything's good. These are individual events. So, Chase Manhattan Bank, JPMorgan, it goes out. Somebody else goes out. And I also think that, the press is sort of having a lot of fun with it," Trump said.

On Thursday, JPMorgan Chase disclosed that third-party service providers working with the financial institution were targeted in a cyberattack, with reports indicating that data, including email addresses and phone numbers, belonging to around 16,000 of its wealthy customers was exposed by a ransomware group.

According to Fox News, a ransomware group identified as non-profit claimed responsibility for leaking data belonging to customers of JPMorgan Chase, Visa and Mastercard.

The breach reportedly involved third-party business partners and exposed customer email addresses, phone numbers and account IDs.

In a post on X, JPMorgan on Thursday (local time) said it had learned that third parties providing services to the firm had been targeted in a cyberattack. The bank said its investigation suggested that attackers had accessed certain marketing data held by those vendors, which may have included customer names and email addresses.

The latest incidents involving JPMorgan come amid several other technology-related disruptions in recent weeks, including a nationwide Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) ground stop that affected air travel last week and a global email outage at Microsoft. Last month, cryptocurrency exchange Binance also experienced a major cyberattack.

data.title: Arizona investigating OpenAI, other firms over possible rogue agents
data.description:
By David Thomas The state of Arizona ??has opened a criminal investigation into  OpenAI and other AI companies relating to the "apparent infiltration of banks by rogue AI agents," ??Arizona Attorney General Kris Mayes said Wednesday. 
A criminal investigation does not necessarily mean charges will be brought. Mayes said her office was investigating whether Arizona ‌state law was being violated  on an ongoing basis. 
"The  state of Arizona is very worried about this, and we  are looking at it from multiple angles," Mayes told a press conference in Chicago. 
Mayes declined to identify the other companies her office was investigating. She said her office had been in contact with Arizona banks,  but declined to name them or give their responses. 
 
A spokesperson for ‌OpenAI did not immediately respond to a request for comment. 
The banking  industry has become increasingly concerned that sophisticated AI agents could harm the banking system and the institutions trusted to hold people's wealth. Reuters reported last month that ‌major US banks have  been blocking third-party AI agents from ‌operating inside customer accounts and making transactions. 
Mayes' comments come two ‌days ??after California Attorney General Rob Bonta sued OpenAI for allegedly developing  a dangerous product without adequate safety procedures or oversight after reports that its AI models had carried out cyberattacks independently. 
OpenAI  did not immediately respond to a Reuters request for comment on that lawsuit, but the company has acknowledged ‌a general need for more transparency around rogue AI behavior and said ‌it was reinforcing its safeguards. On September 16, the company published a new framework for disclosing such incidents, saying it would err on the side of transparency "even when significance is uncertain."

data.title: Nearly nine months on, BIRAC yet to name startups under RDI fund
data.description:
It has been nearly nine months since the Biotechnology Industry Research Assistance Council (BIRAC), a second-level fund manager, opened its first call for proposals for biotechnology (bi­otech) startups under the Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) fund. Yet, no formal announcement on the selected startups has been made. 
While the Technology Development Board (TDB), another second-level fund manager, has announced its first cohort of companies and is preparing to select the second, BIRAC has yet to make a formal announcement, despite having shortlisted seven to eight companies. 
A detailed email sent to the Department of Science and Technology and BIRAC seeking an update on the selection process, reasons for the delay and expected disbursement timelines did not elicit a response. 
One of the sticking points has been the funding structure, said some founders. Unlike TDB, which is extending low-interest loans, BIRAC has proposed a combination of debt and equity financing. According to several founders, negotiations have dragged on over the investment terms and the extent of equity dilution that startups may have to accept. 
At the launch of the call for proposals in February this year, BIRAC had said the evaluation of applications would be completed within eight weeks of receiving proposals, with funds expected to be disbursed within 12 weeks of evaluation. However, the process has dragged on well beyond the stipulated timelines. 
A person at BIRAC involved in the selection process said, “The funding structure is an important consideration. While low-interest loans offer a relati­vely straightforward financing route, a combination of debt and equity requires clarity on valuation, dilution, and other terms. That is why negotiations are taking longer than anticipated.” 
BIRAC’s relative inexperien­ce in structuring debt and equity investments is also understood to have contributed to the delay. Traditionally, the organisation has operated largely as a grant-giving institution. Working out investment term sheets and agreements under the RDI framework is taking additional time, sources said. 
However, several sources familiar with the process said the applications were in the final stage, with the finer details of the agreements being ironed out. The formal announcement is likely to follow once the agreements are finalised. 
The delay, meanwhile, has been weighing on startups awaiting funding, particularly those working on capital-intensive biotech projects. One founder, whose startup is part of the maiden cohort, said rising costs of manpower, equipment, and raw materials had pushed up project expenses. 
“Compared with the beginning of the year, when we submitted our applications and detailed our project plans, expenses have risen by around 10 per cent. The uncertainty over the timing of funding has complicated financial planning,” the founder said. “By the time the funding comes through, the original project cost estimates may no longer hold.” 
Another founder raised concerns over the uncertainty surrounding limited partner commitments, which were based on earlier business valuations and revenue projections. 
“The commitments were made based on certain valuations and revenue projections. With the funding process getting delayed, those assumptions are changing. It creates uncertainty for both the startup and the investors who are expected to participate,” the founder said. 
The RDI framework provides financing of up to 50 per cent of the assessed project cost, with startups required to arrange the remaining amount through self-financing or commercial sources. 
Consequently, a few startups have written separately to BIRAC, flagging concerns over the delay and seeking clarity on disbursement timelines. Some founders said they received tim­ely responses, while others poin­ted to delays in communication.
“There has been very little communication on the status of applications. We (startups) have invested considerable time and resources in preparing proposals, but there is no clear mechanism to track the status of applications or when a decision can be expected. We do not even know the complete list of companies selected for the first cohort,” one of the founders quoted above added. 
While several government schemes provide adequate data on their respective websites to showcase progress, the RDI fund does not have a publicly accessible dashboard tracking applications received, shortlisted, approved, and funded.

data.title: AI trade unwinds; India emerges as a diversification opportunity: Brokerage
data.description:
Disclaimer: This article is written by Choice Institutional Equities. Views expressed are his own. Readers' discretion is advised.
 
The global investment landscape is witnessing a shift as investors reassess their exposure to the AI-led rally and increasingly seek opportunities beyond the technology investment cycle. After attracting significant capital into AI-linked companies, particularly in the US, Taiwan and South Korea, concerns around elevated valuations, higher debt and sustainability of returns are prompting investors to reassess crowded positions. This rotation could create an opportunity for India, which offers relatively lower direct exposure to the global AI trade and diversified domestic earnings drivers.
 
The AI investment cycle spans five layers: energy, data centres and networks, compute, models and applications. While substantial capital has flowed into semiconductors, GPUs and foundation models, infrastructure constraints across power generation, transmission, cooling and data-centre capacity highlight that AI is as much an industrial and energy investment cycle as a technology one. India offers opportunities across power infrastructure, industrials, data centres and technology, while its limited exposure to the global semiconductor ecosystem provides diversification from the crowded AI trade.
 
 
However, the emerging anti-AI trade should not be interpreted as a bet against technology. Rather, it represents an opportunity to invest in businesses whose earnings growth is driven by independent domestic and sectoral factors. Banking and financial services, automobiles, consumer discretionary, healthcare, telecom, capital goods and infrastructure offer diversified growth opportunities supported by domestic demand, credit expansion, manufacturing investments and capital expenditure.
 
India's positioning is particularly relevant given the concentration of global AI investments. The US attracted approximately US$194bn, or 75 per cent of global AI venture-capital deal value in 2025, while Taiwan and South Korea benefited disproportionately from the AI-led rally. In contrast, India's diversified market composition offers exposure to multiple earnings drivers beyond the AI investment cycle. ALSO READ: AI sell-off hits Indian smallcaps; Sterlite, HFCL down up to 29% in a month
 
Foreign investor sentiment towards India has improved meaningfully: FPIs recorded net equity inflows of approximately INR 89,856 Cr. during November up to November 17, reversing outflows of INR 34,843 Cr. in October and INR 35,861 Cr. in September. The Nifty 50 closed at 25,387 on November 17, while softer crude prices, with Brent around US$93/barrel, provided an additional macroeconomic tailwind.
 
Domestic fundamentals are also showing resilience: Q2FY27 results for Nifty 50 companies (excluding financials) reflected healthy operating performance, with revenue and PAT growing 24.1 per cent and 27.6 per cent YoY, respectively. Revenue and EBITDA exceeded our estimates by 6.3 per cent and 8.1 per cent, respectively, with EBITDA growing 23.2 per cent YoY. This suggests that domestic demand has remained resilient despite the prolonged geopolitical conflict.
 
Overall, the unwinding of the global AI trade presents India with an opportunity to emerge as a natural diversification destination. Importantly, both investment themes can coexist. India can participate in the AI opportunity through select technology, power, capital goods and data-centre businesses, while banking, consumption, healthcare, industrial and infrastructure sectors offer independent earnings growth. This combination could strengthen India's appeal as a long-term destination for global capital, with sustained earnings delivery, reasonable valuations and macroeconomic stability remaining critical to a durable market re-rating.
